description: Somos un grupo de Él Volcán, San Luis, interesados en el bienestar del planeta, la implementación de nuevas tecnologías y el desarrollo de software. Queremos aprovechar esta oportunidad para utilizar nuestras habilidades y mejorar al mundo.
summary: EDUCABASE is an educational video game for kids aged 7 to 12 that puts them in charge of a base on the Moon. Every turn, something based on real science happens (a solar storm, the lunar night, a micrometeorite, ice in a crater) and the player must choose what to do. Each decision changes the base’s oxygen, radiation and energy, showing the trade-offs astronauts face every day to keep a mission running and themselves safe. Some events use real NASA data, such as solar flares from DONKI and radiation measured around the Moon (RadLab). After each choice, an animation and a “Did you know?” fact explain the science, so kids learn by deciding.
details:
EDUCABASE is a choice-making game that teaches kids about space missions and the decisions astronauts make on a daily basis to keep the mission running and themselves safe. The player manages a lunar base through events drawn from a pool of 72, each based on real science and NASA missions (Apollo, Artemis II, LRO, Blue Ghost, the International Space Station). Each choice changes three indicators (oxygen, radiation and energy) plus the base’s vitality, so kids learn that every solution has a cost.

Features: Three difficulty levels (1, 5, and 10 years), plus a fourth unlockable level that makes the game much harder, real space-weather data from NASA DONKI and real lunar radiation measurements from RadLab, a cartoon animation for every answer, a “Did you know?” science fact, a glossary of space words written for kids, a collection that fills up with the questions the player has solved, a help mode, a tutorial, and full English and Spanish versions. It can be played directly in the browser on itch.io, and there is also a Windows version.

It was made with Godot Engine 4.3 (GDScript) and Python. All graphics and animations are drawn with code in a minimalist, colorful style that appeals to young players, and the music is original, generated with code. The gameplay is inspired by card-choice games like “Reigns”, turning real space problems into simple decisions with real consequences.

Use of AI: Claude (Anthropic) helped write and debug the code, the animations, the music-generation script, the texts and their translation. The team reviewed and validated all the content.
